What is the theme? These seven paragraphs were written by different sages and eventually were put together to form the “long Tachanun,” which is why you will find that many of the ideas and themes repeat themselves. The basic theme is that Hashem is our only hope for salvation from the suffering that we have brought upon ourselves through not living up to our mission to the world. As contrasted with the “short Tachanun,” which is personal in nature (and said every weekday), the “long Tachanun” focuses on our communal pain, and the desecrated status of Yerushalayim, our holy city. Since the wording of the seven paragraphs of “long Tachanun” is quite straightforward and understandable, we will simply point out the key themes of each paragraph.
